what_it_does: PED is the layer that turns raw sensor collection (full-motion video, EO/IR still imagery, SAR, SIGINT/ELINT cues, radar tracks, OSINT/PAI) into usable intelligence products and machine-readable tracks/detections. Processing = format conversion, georegistration, orthorectification, decompression and metadata normalization (e.g., MISB KLV, NITF/GeoTIFF, STANAG 4607 GMTI). Exploitation = human and algorithmic detection, classification, identification, change detection, track initiation/maintenance, multi-INT correlation, and analyst judgement producing reports, target packets and annotated products. Dissemination = pushing products, alerts and tracks to consumers (targeting cells, fires systems, common operating pictures, coalition partners) across security domains and bandwidth-limited links. The 2024-2026 shift is from human-in-the-loop 'ISR analysis' to platform-mediated, AI-assisted workflows (Maven Smart System, TITAN, AIDP) that must run from enterprise cloud to disconnected tactical nodes.

sub_taxonomy.name: Imagery/FMV computer vision (detection, classification, change detection)
sub_taxonomy.note: Object/event detection on EO/IR/SAR and FMV; the most commoditized algorithmic sub-layer (Maven, RAIC Labs, BlackSky Spectra, Matroid). Data and labeling access, not model architecture, is the differentiator.

sub_taxonomy.name: GEOINT commercial analytics (facility monitoring, feature extraction, economic indicators)
sub_taxonomy.note: NGA's Luno A (imagery analysis) and Luno B (commercial AI products) are the buying vehicles; vendors are largely imagery operators (BlackSky, Ursa Space) and analytics firms.

sub_taxonomy.name: Multi-INT / track fusion and target development
sub_taxonomy.note: Correlating detections and tracks across sensors into targetable entities; TITAN and Maven Smart System own this at division/corps and joint echelons. Fusion is where classification and program-of-record ownership are heaviest.

sub_taxonomy.name: Analyst workflow, collaboration, automated reporting and prioritization
sub_taxonomy.note: Tasking-to-product workflow tooling, alerts, queue prioritization, report generation; historically DCGS-A/AF DCGS/DCGS-N; now Maven Smart System, AIDP (Palantir), Vannevar Labs. This is where 'swivel-chair' pain is documented (MIPB 2026).

sub_taxonomy.name: Edge / DDIL PED (on-platform and tactical-node processing, data reduction)
sub_taxonomy.note: Processing at or near the sensor to reduce bandwidth and work disconnected; AIDP's 2026 Call for Solutions explicitly requires 72-hour autonomous operation on tactical edge nodes with later sync to Maven. Fewest scaled products; most startup-shaped.

sub_taxonomy.name: AI/ML lifecycle for PED models (labeling, T&E, deployment, drift)
sub_taxonomy.note: Army's Project Linchpin (PM IS&A) and Maven's model onboarding (Open DAGIR) define this; it is an enabling sub-layer rather than an end-user product.

current_architecture.description: A three-tier architecture is emerging: (1) an enterprise AI/data layer (NGA Maven models and data; Maven Smart System as the joint/COCOM analytic and targeting platform; Open DAGIR for third-party apps), (2) service intelligence platforms (Army AIDP replacing DCGS-A; TITAN ground stations at division/corps/MDTF; AF DCGS Open Architecture; DCGS-N), and (3) commercial analytics feeds (NGA Luno A/B, Space Force commercial ISR) plus a thin, fragmented tactical-edge tier (TAK plugins, vendor edge boxes). Palantir is prime on MSS, AIDP and TITAN, giving one vendor the integration seams between all three tiers (FACT for prime roles; INFERENCE on the consequences).

technical_difficulty.summary: Detection models on imagery are commoditized; the hard parts are (a) operating with sparse, shifting, classified training data, (b) robust georegistration and track continuity across sensors, (c) running and updating models on constrained edge hardware without connectivity, (d) integrating into Maven/AIDP/TITAN data models and cross-domain guards, and (e) earning analyst trust (calibration, provenance, low false-alarm rates). Difficulty: medium for a niche edge or workflow product; very high for a fusion/targeting platform.
required_expertise: computer vision on EO/IR/SAR/FMV incl. MISB metadata handling
edge ML deployment and model compression (Jetson/Xavier-class, FPGA-optional)
distributed systems with intermittent sync (CRDT-style or store-and-forward)
intelligence analysis tradecraft and targeting workflow
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Delivering trustworthy, low-false-alarm detections and consistent tracks under DDIL conditions with models that must be trained on data the startup cannot access until it is already inside a program - a data-access chicken-and-egg that favors Palantir, NGA-Maven and imagery operators.
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: Object detectors (YOLO/DETR families), foundation vision models, orthorectification libraries (GDAL), STAC catalogs, TAK plugins, Kafka/streaming, cloud IL5 hosting patterns, MISB KLV parsers.

capital_intensity.proof_of_concept_usd: $100k-$400k (commercial imagery and open FMV datasets, cloud GPUs, 2-3 engineers for 6-9 months)
capital_intensity.credible_military_demo_usd: $1M-$4M (SBIR Phase II or OTA-scale: rugged edge hardware, exercise participation such as Scarlet Dragon/PC-C, IL5 hosting, initial ATO artifacts, one FSE, Secret-cleared staff)
capital_intensity.first_production_deployment_usd: $5M-$25M (cATO/ATO on SIPR, SCIF/facility clearance, cleared engineers, 24/7 support, MSS/AIDP integration certification, multi-site fielding)
capital_intensity.assumptions: Software-only product; no proprietary sensors; leverages commercial imagery for PoC; assumes onboarding through Open DAGIR or AIDP subcontract rather than standalone program; ranges are INFERENCE from SBIR/OTA sizes seen (Danti $1.2M/$1.9M; TITAN prototype $178M at platform scale).

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: partly - commercial EO/SAR imagery, open FMV datasets and NGA Luno-style unclassified analytics allow a real PoC; but tactical FMV, SIGINT cues and targeting workflows are not reproducible without government data.
regulatory_access.government_data_required: Yes for anything beyond commercial GEOINT: MISB FMV from RPAs, TITAN/AIDP data models, labeled military datasets (Maven/Linchpin). Access usually comes only via SBIR Phase II, OTA or a prime's subcontract.
regulatory_access.itar_ear: Software specially designed for military ISR exploitation or targeting can be a defense article/technical data under ITAR (e.g., USML Cat XI) or fall under EAR 600-series/other ECCNs; a non-US-person founder or engineer triggers deemed-export analysis. Requires specialist export-control counsel before any government data or spec is shared with non-US persons.
regulatory_access.cui_likely: Yes - nearly all program documentation (AIDP CfS attachments, GFI lists, product demonstration plans) is CUI; requires NIST 800-171/CMMC posture.
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: Yes - MSS, TITAN and AIDP operate at Secret/TS; production deployment requires cleared personnel, facility clearance (FCL) and likely a cross-domain path.
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: Not strictly required for a commercial-imagery MVP or SBIR Phase I; required by Phase II/OTA demo stage for FMV/targeting work (INFERENCE from program security domains).
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: An Indonesian founder who is not a US person cannot hold a US security clearance, would be a deemed-export concern for ITAR/EAR technical data, and could trigger FOCI review for facility clearance if holding significant ownership/control. The German founder's status improves after permanent residency for export purposes (US person) but clearances generally require citizenship. Mitigations (segregated corporate structure, US-person control, proxy/SSA agreements) exist but need FOCI/export counsel; this is a first-order constraint for S04 specifically because the valuable data and integration points are classified.

unsolved_pain.label: FACT (award); INFERENCE (unsolved at scale)

unsolved_pain.pain: Command and control integration across services remains incomplete, affecting how intelligence products reach decision makers.
unsolved_pain.evidence: GAO-25-106454 'Defense Command and Control: Further Progress Hinges on Establishing...' (2025) finds continued gaps in DoD's C2 modernization governance.
unsolved_pain.label: FACT

why_not_solved.explanation: Palantir is prime on MSS, AIDP and TITAN; integration seams, ontologies and app-onboarding are controlled by one vendor and the government's Open DAGIR effort is the only counterweight. Startups must build on, not around, this.

Military FMV, SAR, SIGINT cues and labeled targeting data live on SIPR/JWICS; models cannot be trained or validated on them without being inside a program. Commercial imagery is available but is where imagery operators already bundle analytics.
Production PED runs at Secret/TS; cleared staff, facility clearance and cross-domain approvals gate every deployment, adding 12-24 months and millions in cost.
Dozens of formats (MISB, NITF, STANAG 4607/4676, CoT, Link 16, USMTF) and legacy DCGS interfaces; the 'swivel chair' problem is an integration and governance failure more than an algorithm failure.
Foundation vision models, few-shot detection and edge inference hardware capable of DDIL operation matured only 2022-2025; the requirements (AIDP 72-hour autonomy) are being written in 2026.
Army (AIDP/TITAN), CDAO (MSS), NGA (Luno), AF (DCGS/AFWERX), Navy (DCGS-N) buy separately; small vendors accumulate SBIRs across buyers without a single transition owner.

Task orders for commercial analytics are tens of millions spread across 10-13 vendors; sustaining a cleared engineering team on that revenue is marginal, which is why several startups (Rebellion, Primer) retreated.

attractiveness.bull: Real production money is arriving (TITAN $192M, MSS program of record, Luno TOs) and OSD is mandating consolidation, which creates an app-ecosystem opportunity (Open DAGIR, AIDP 'partner environments' and edge nodes) where small vendors can plug specialized capabilities into a funded platform. DDIL edge PED and workflow automation are explicitly demanded in 2026 solicitations and are not owned by a scaled startup. Commercial imagery allows an unclassified MVP.
attractiveness.bear: The layer is consolidating around Palantir/Anduril with government backing; startups without clearances and government data are structurally locked out of the valuable (classified, fused, targeting) parts. Commercial-analytics niches are crowded by imagery operators and 23 Luno vendors, task orders are small, and SBIR-only companies (Danti, RAIC) show proto-purgatory. For this founder team, the non-US-person constraint hits S04 harder than most segments.
attractiveness.verdict: Medium-low overall; medium for a narrow DDIL-edge or analyst-workflow component sold into AIDP/MSS/TAK ecosystems; low for anything platform-shaped or targeting-adjacent.

MSS $480M contract; Open DAGIR launched (follow-on / ecosystem)

market_stage.rationale: The full RFI -> prototype -> production -> repeat sequence is visible for the platform tier (Maven, TITAN) within 2022-2026, so the segment is past prototyping for incumbents. The edge/DDIL and commercial-analytics tiers are earlier: AIDP-Next is at Call-for-Solutions stage (2026) and Luno is in first-round task orders. Hence 'Transitioning' overall with sub-tier variation.

proto_purgatory.notes: Small vendors show the pattern: Danti (D2P2 2023 -> TACFI 2024 -> AF contract 2025, no PoR), RAIC Labs (AFWERX 2021 -> Army SBIR Phase I), Matroid (AF SBIR), Edgybees/Reveal (multiple SBIR/OTA cycles, no verified 2025-2026 production). By contrast Palantir, Anduril and Vannevar reached production via OTA/consolidated vehicles. NGA explicitly worries about transitioning Luno capabilities into production.
proto_purgatory.opportunity_or_warning: Warning for standalone point-solution startups; opportunity only if the go-to-market is designed from day one around a transition owner (Open DAGIR onboarding to MSS, AIDP subcontract, TAK product line, or a prime's production program) rather than accumulating SBIRs.

exercise_evidence.quote_or_paraphrase: AI flew aboard an RAAF P-8A for the first time, assisting aircrew in real time by analysing data; first deployment of agentic AI (Vannevar Labs) alongside planners and operators. Coalition setting implies releasability constraints on AI-derived products (INFERENCE; Vannevar blog not fetchable this session).

Objective to enhance interoperability on a common operating platform, incorporating real-time tracking and engagement of UAS; series exists to use AI to share data more efficiently from sensor to shooter.

candidate_gaps.title: Autonomous DDIL edge PED node with resilient sync to AIDP/Maven
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Tactical intelligence nodes cannot process, exploit and locally fuse organic sensor data for 72+ hours while disconnected and then reconcile cleanly with enterprise platforms when links return.
candidate_gaps.user: Brigade/battalion S2 sections, MDTF and SOF intelligence teams, small-UAS operators
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Organic sensors (small UAS, ground sensors, radios) record locally; 2) when a link exists, raw video/imagery is pushed to brigade or enterprise DCGS-A/AIDP or Maven; 3) enterprise models detect/annotate; 4) analyst reviews and builds products; 5) products are pushed back down over the same congested link; 6) when disconnected, steps 2-5 stall and analysts screen video manually and hand-plot in TAK or slides.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: AIDP (Palantir) with limited edge kits; TITAN Basic variants at division; vendor point tools (Reveal Farsight, Edgybees, Overwatch on-platform); TAK plugins; manual screening.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: No fielded product provides local inference, local track fusion, prioritized data reduction and conflict-free bidirectional sync to MSS/AIDP under DDIL; AIDP CfS (July 2026) writes this as a new requirement.

evidence.claim: AIDP Call for Solutions requires 72-hour autonomous operation on tactical edge nodes in DDIL and bi-directional data exchange with Maven Smart System.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: AIDP RFI #4 states requirement focuses on intelligence capabilities from enterprise cloud to tactical edge including DDIL environments.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Army is buying TITAN Basic variants specifically for faster deployment and mobility, indicating demand for lighter, forward processing.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Open DAGIR has an 'edge data integration services' line of effort, i.e., CDAO acknowledges edge integration as unsolved.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Multiple startups (Reveal, Edgybees, Overwatch, Latent AI) attempt partial edge-PED solutions; none evidenced at production scale.
evidence.label: INFERENCE (RECALL, LOW)

evidence.claim: Analysts manually move data between disconnected systems ('swivel chair').
evidence.label: FACT

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Requires simultaneous mastery of edge ML, sync semantics, MISB/CoT/AIDP data models and access to military sensor data and networks; the integration target (AIDP/MSS APIs) is controlled by Palantir and only now being opened; SBIR-sized money cannot fund cleared field engineering.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: High - AIDP-Next incumbent (likely Palantir) and Anduril will claim the edge node in their proposals; a startup survives only as an onboarded component or via TAK/TITAN Basic subcontract.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: A small, hardware-agnostic 'intel edge runtime' that runs curated detection/track models on Jetson-class hardware, does prioritized data reduction (send detections + chips, not video), keeps a local conflict-free store, and exposes CoT/TAK and an AIDP/MSS-compatible sync adapter.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Commercial small-UAS FMV + open EO datasets; run detector + tracker on Jetson Orin; local web UI for S2; CoT out to ATAK; store-and-forward sync to a mock 'enterprise' STAC/PostGIS; demonstrate 72-hour disconnected operation and clean reconciliation with 5% bandwidth.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Unclassified FMV/EO for MVP; MISB-compliant military FMV and AIDP data model access for credible demo (requires SBIR Phase II/OTA or prime partnership).
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: TAK/CoT, MISB KLV, STANAG 4676 tracks, AIDP/MSS APIs (Open DAGIR onboarding), IL5/SIPR ATO path.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: Army SBIR/xTech, DIU CSO on edge AI, AIDP-Next subcontract, TAK plugin, Open DAGIR onboarding.
candidate_gaps.why_now: AIDP-Next requirements (2026) and TITAN production create an explicit, funded need; edge inference hardware and foundation models make 72-hour autonomy feasible.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Palantir/Anduril bundle the edge node into AIDP/TITAN and close the API; non-US-person founder blocks access to military FMV and networks.

candidate_gaps.title: Swivel-chair elimination: automated cross-system intel product generation with provenance
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Analysts at brigade-to-corps re-enter detections, tracks and assessments across AIDP/DCGS-A, MSS, fires C2, chat and briefing slides because no tool produces standardized, provenance-tracked products consumable by each system.
candidate_gaps.user: 35F/35G analysts and targeting officers at brigade, division, corps and COCOM J2
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Receive cues from Maven/AIDP, chat, email; 2) verify in imagery tool; 3) manually build target graphic and INTSUM slides; 4) re-type entity data into fires C2 and COP; 5) post to chat; 6) repeat each battle-rhythm cycle.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: MSS and AIDP dashboards; PowerPoint; chat (MS Teams/Mattermost/mIRC); manual USMTF/VMF entry; contractor FSEs.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Integration and governance: products are not machine-readable across systems; provenance and releasability are lost; OSD's forced migration to MSS (2026) is the top-down answer but leaves gaps at echelons below division and in fires/COP handoffs.

evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: OSD directs components to migrate C2/analytic tools onto MSS on an aggressive timeline - government acknowledges duplication and disconnection.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.label: FACT

evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Vannevar Labs' agentic AI at Talisman Sabre 2025 and DIU production transition show buyers paying for analyst-workflow automation.
evidence.label: FACT

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Requires deep access to the actual systems (SIPR, AIDP, AFATDS) and their message formats; the natural owner is now the MSS/AIDP prime; a startup's product would be an 'app' inside someone else's platform with thin margins.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: Very high - this is core roadmap for Palantir and Vannevar; OSD consolidation reduces the number of seams a startup could sit in.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: LLM-driven product generator that ingests structured detections/tracks and free-text chat and emits standard products (USMTF/VMF messages, CoT, INTSUM sections, target packets) with per-claim provenance and releasability markings; deployable as Open DAGIR app.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Unclassified exercise-style synthetic data; generate INTSUM and target nomination from detection feeds and chat logs; show round-trip into TAK and a mock AFATDS message; measure analyst time saved with veteran analysts.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Real chat logs, INTSUM templates, unit SOPs - CUI at minimum; classified for realistic evaluation.
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: MSS/Open DAGIR onboarding, AIDP APIs, USMTF/VMF, TAK; IL5/SIPR ATO.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: Open DAGIR onboarding, Army xTech/SBIR, direct sale to XVIII Airborne Corps innovation cell, partnership with Vannevar/BigBear.
candidate_gaps.why_now: LLM product generation is credible in 2025-2026 and OSD consolidation defines a single API target (MSS).
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: MSS native features absorb it; classification blocks a non-US founder from the data needed to make it good.

candidate_gaps.title: Luno-to-enterprise transition layer: productionizing commercial GEOINT analytics inside government systems
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: NGA buys commercial analytics via Luno A/B task orders but struggles to integrate outputs into enterprise systems and transition them to sustained production use.
candidate_gaps.user: NGA analysts and Luno program office; combatant command GEOINT cells consuming commercial products
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) NGA issues task order for a monitoring problem; 2) vendor delivers analytics via its own portal/API; 3) government must map outputs into NGA enterprise/Maven data models; 4) integration is bespoke per vendor; 5) production transition slips.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Vendor portals, NGA integration staff and contractors, Maven onboarding pathways.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Each of 23 Luno vendors integrates differently; schemas, confidence semantics and provenance are inconsistent; NGA explicitly scheduled awards early to leave time for integration.

evidence.claim: NGA aims to award most Luno TOs by early 2026 to have time to integrate capabilities into enterprise systems and transition to production.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Luno A ($290M, 10 vendors) and Luno B ($200M, 13 vendors) exist with multiple task orders awarded 2025-2026.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Space Force and NGA reached an agreement on purchasing commercial ISR, implying growing volume of commercial analytics needing integration.
evidence.label: FACT

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: It is an integration-services problem inside NGA's enterprise (classified boundaries, government-owned schemas); Palantir/Maven already positions as the integration layer; vendors have no incentive to standardize.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: High - NGA Maven and MSS are the designated integration layer; a startup would compete with government-owned infrastructure.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: A vendor-side 'Luno output normalizer' SDK plus STAC/OGC-compliant product catalog with confidence/provenance schema that vendors adopt to speed government ingestion.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Open-source schema + reference adapters for 3 commercial analytics providers; demo ingest into an open GEOINT viewer; pitch to Luno B vendors as compliance accelerator.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Unclassified commercial analytics outputs (accessible); NGA enterprise schemas (CUI/classified).
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: NGA enterprise/Maven APIs; STAC/OGC; IC ITE cloud.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: Luno B subcontract, NGA SBIR, sell to Luno vendors as B2B tooling.
candidate_gaps.why_now: Luno task orders peaking 2025-2026; NGA voiced the integration concern.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Government solves it with Maven onboarding pathways; market is 23 vendors with small budgets (economics).

candidate_gaps.title: Continuous T&E and drift monitoring for fielded PED computer-vision models
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Fielded detectors degrade with new sensors, theaters and adversary camouflage, and DoD lacks the workforce and tooling to monitor, re-label and re-validate models across programs (Maven, TITAN, AIDP, Linchpin).
candidate_gaps.user: Program AI leads (PM IS&A Linchpin, NGA Maven, CDAO), unit data officers
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Model onboarded to Maven/Linchpin; 2) analysts click-through confirm/reject; 3) feedback aggregated irregularly; 4) retraining by vendor or government team; 5) redeployment via ATO'd pipeline months later.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Project Linchpin pipeline, Maven/NGA labeling contracts (Scale, Enabled Intelligence - RECALL), CDAO T&E frameworks.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Feedback loops are slow and workforce-limited; no independent, cross-program evaluation product evidenced in the open.

candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: Sensor-agnostic drift and false-alarm monitoring that runs on analyst confirm/reject telemetry and flags retraining needs with synthetic-data augmentation.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Open imagery benchmark + drift dashboard; test on public xView/DOTA-style data with simulated theater shift.

candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Government-internal solution; no independent startup market (J).

candidate_gaps.title: Releasability-aware dissemination of AI-derived intelligence to coalition partners
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: AI-generated detections and products cannot be shared quickly with allies because releasability, sanitization and provenance handling are manual and classification-bound.
candidate_gaps.user: Coalition J2 cells, Mission Partner Environment managers, exercise planners (Talisman Sabre, AUKUS)
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) US-only product produced in MSS/AIDP; 2) analyst manually creates releasable version; 3) foreign disclosure officer reviews; 4) product transferred across guard to MPE; 5) partners receive late, stripped products.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Manual FDO workflows, cross-domain solutions, MPE tools, unclassified commercial GEOINT as a workaround.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Policy and classification, not technology; AI outputs lack provenance metadata needed for automated downgrade decisions.
